results.reason: Issue 1 says MSA § 3.2 makes Bellweather the nationwide exclusive provider of all warehousing, freight and delivery services, contrary to Term Sheet § 4.1's NYC-metro last-mile scope. It proposes replacement language tracking the term sheet.

Issue 2 says § 11.3 carves Harrowgate's § 10.2 indemnity out of the cap, while Bellweather's § 10.1 indemnity stays capped at 12 months' fees. It explains the one-sided unlimited exposure and recommends deleting the carve-out or making it mutual.

Issue 3 identifies DPA § 9.1's Delaware law and Wilmington forum and the conflict with MSA § 18.1 New York. It states that the DPA prevails under MSA § 2.3 and recommends conforming the DPA to MSA § 18.
Issue 4 identifies the 3-year auto-renewals with a 15-day notice window and explains the lock-in risk. It recommends 1-year renewals, 90-day notice, a reminder notice and termination for convenience.
The response never addresses SOW § 8.2 or the asymmetric assignment rights against MSA § 17.4.
It quotes MSA § 2.3: 'the Data Processing Addendum, then this Agreement, then the Statement of Work.'
It states the cap is 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim' (§ 11.1).
It is a memo to the Supervising Partner. Each issue gives Where, What it says, Why it matters and Recommended fix.
The issues are expressly ordered by importance, and Part IV lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The response concludes that the DPA's Delaware clause controls data disputes and that the documents conflict.
The response states that the exclusivity clause is far broader than the term sheet.
